title: Highway drive
topic: A friend averages two driving speeds from a holiday trip
blurb: A friend is recapping their Sunday night drive home.
prompt: A friend just sent this in the group chat. Tap a line if something doesn't add up, or let it pass.

segments.label: The drive
segments.text: Drove home from my sister's last night — left right at 6:00, pulled into the driveway at 8:00, no stops.

segments.label: The split
segments.text: Crawled at 40 mph until 7:00 in holiday traffic, then cruised at 70 mph the rest of the way.

segments.label: The math
segments.text: 40 and 70 averages out to 55, so I did 55 mph overall — 110 miles door to door.

segments.label: The brag
segments.text: Way better than last Christmas when it took almost three hours.

conclusion: 40 mph until 7:00 and 70 mph until 8:00 averages to 55 mph and 110 miles total.

diagnosis: Saying 'two hours straight' hides ramp and city slowdowns, so a single average speed can't be trusted.
A round trip from a relative's house needs both directions before you can quote an average pace.
Two hours is rounded to the nearest whole hour, which breaks the 110-mile calculation.
Without knowing the total highway mileage first, you can't split the trip into two equal hours.
fix: Give the exact odometer reading before estimating any speed.
Break the two hours into city minutes and highway minutes separately.
Log the gas-station pause time even if you stayed in the car.
Wait until you drive back to average both directions together.

diagnosis: You spend more miles at 70 mph than at 40 mph, so splitting the trip by time instead of distance distorts the pace.
Switching straight from 40 mph to 70 mph ignores acceleration time, so the two hours can't add up cleanly.
Holiday traffic fluctuates constantly, so quoting 40 mph for an hour makes the second hour's 70 mph unusable.
The two legs cover unequal distances (40 vs 70 miles), so you can't combine them into one trip average.
fix: Split the trip into two equal 55-mile halves before comparing speeds.
Account for the time spent accelerating from 40 mph up to 70 mph.
Use the median speed across the two hours instead of two flat numbers.
Weight the 40 mph leg higher because slow traffic takes longer per mile.

diagnosis: You can't take a plain average of two speeds — the true average of 40 and 70 mph is about 50.9 mph, around 102 miles.
The 40 mph leg drags the overall speed below 55 mph because slower driving always carries heavier weight.
55 mph over two hours is 110 miles, but 40 plus 70 already gave you the distance, not the speed.
Averaging 40 and 70 only works if both halves of the road were the exact same length in miles.
fix: Use 2 × 40 × 70 / (40 + 70) ≈ 50.9 mph, which puts the drive at roughly 102 miles.
Weight each speed by its share of the miles driven, giving closer to 51 mph.
Divide 110 miles by the slower speed first to check whether two hours is enough.
Report the two legs separately because speeds never average linearly.

diagnosis: Averaging under 51 mph on a Sunday highway isn't fast once you fix the speed formula.
Sunday traffic is usually lighter than Friday, so 55 mph is actually below normal highway speed.
Claiming 'not bad' ignores that the first half of the drive was 40 mph bumper-to-bumper.
Calling 110 miles in two hours 'not bad' assumes the speed limit was 55 mph the whole way.
fix: Compare against your usual weekday time on the same route instead.
Re-check the total with ~51 mph before calling the trip quick.
Note how many miles were stuck at 40 mph before bragging about the pace.
Leave an hour earlier next Sunday so both hours run near 70 mph.

clean_segments: Drove home from my sister's last night — left right at 6:00, pulled into the driveway at 8:00, no stops.
Crawled at 40 mph until 7:00 in holiday traffic, then cruised at 70 mph the rest of the way.
40 and 70 averages out to 55, so I did 55 mph overall — 110 miles door to door.
Way better than last Christmas when it took almost three hours.
clean_conclusion: The plain average actually works here — the two legs lasted the same amount of time (an hour each), not the same distance. 40 miles plus 70 miles in 2 hours really is 55 mph.
